tools.name: hasdata_google_travel_hotels_getGoogleHotels
tools.desc:
Get Google Hotels Results

Searches Google Hotels for hotels and vacation rentals with check-in/check-out dates, guest m
tools.description:
Get Google Hotels Results

Searches Google Hotels for hotels and vacation rentals with check-in/check-out dates, guest mix (adults, children with ages), localization (country, language, currency), and advanced filters: price range, property types, amenities, minimum rating, brands, hotel class, free cancellation, special offers, eco-certified, vacation rentals only, bedrooms, bathrooms, and sort order (lowest price, highest rating, most reviewed). Returns per-property name, description, link, GPS coordinates, check-in/out times, rate per night and total rate, price comparisons across sources, hotel class, overall rating, reviews, location rating, images, amenities, nearby places, deals, eco-certification, and pagination tokens. Use for travel research agents, hotel rate monitoring, OTA dashboards, and competitive analysis of accommodations across markets.

parameters.name: adults
parameters.description: Number of adult guests (1-6).

parameters.name: amenity__
parameters.description:
List of amenities to filter by (e.g., `hotelFreeWifi,hotelPool`).

Values prefixed `hotel*` apply when searching hotels (the default mode). Values prefixed `rental*` apply when `vacationRentals=true`.

The two sets are disjoint because Google Hotels exposes different amenity catalogs for each mode — pass values matching the mode you're querying.

parameters.name: bathrooms
parameters.description: Minimum number of bathrooms (vacation rentals only).

parameters.name: bedrooms
parameters.description: Minimum number of bedrooms (vacation rentals only).

parameters.name: brands
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of brand IDs to filter by. Brand IDs are returned in the response under `brands` for the same query.

parameters.name: checkOutDate
parameters.description: The check-out date in 'yyyy-MM-dd' format.

parameters.name: children
parameters.description: Number of child guests (1-5). Total guests (adults + children) cannot exceed 6.

parameters.name: childrenAges
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of children ages (e.g., `5,8,12`). Must match the number of children.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Parameter defines the currency of the returned prices Provide one exact documented value (71 allowed), e.g. `ALL`, `DZD`.

parameters.name: ecoCertified

parameters.name: freeCancellation

parameters.name: gl

parameters.name: hl
parameters.description: The two-letter language code for the language you want to use for the search. Provide one exact documented value (159 allowed), e.g. `af`, `ak`.

parameters.name: hotelClass
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of hotel star classes to include (e.g., `2,3,4,5`).

parameters.name: maxPrice
parameters.description: Maximum price per night, in the selected currency.

parameters.name: minPrice
parameters.description: Minimum price per night, in the selected currency.

parameters.name: nextPageToken
parameters.description: Token to fetch the next page of hotel results. Returned in the `pagination` field of a previous response.

parameters.name: propertyToken
parameters.description: Token used to retrieve details for a specific property. Returned in each property in the results.

parameters.name: propertyType__
parameters.description:
List of property types to filter by (e.g., `hotelResort,hotelMotel`).

Values prefixed `hotel*` apply when searching hotels (the default mode). Values prefixed `rental*` apply when `vacationRentals=true`.

The two sets are disjoint because Google Hotels exposes different property-type catalogs for each mode — pass values matching the mode you're querying.

parameters.name: vacationRentals
parameters.description: Search vacation rentals instead of hotels.

tools.description:

parameters.description: Adult Content Filtering option.

parameters.name: tbs
parameters.description:
`tbs` parameter for the Google Images API customizes image search results with various filters that can be combined using commas. Here are the available options:

Image Size Filters:
  - `isz:l` - Search for large images.
  - `isz:m` - Search for medium images.
  - `isz:i` - Search for icon-sized images.
  - `isz:lt,islt:qsvga` - Filter for images larger than 400×300.
  - `isz:lt,islt:vga` - Filter for images larger than 640×480.
  - `isz:lt,islt:svga` - Filter for images larger than 800×600.
  - `isz:lt,islt:xga` - Filter for images larger than 1024×768.
  - `isz:lt,islt:2mp` - Filter for images larger than 1600×1200.
  - `isz:lt,islt:4mp` - Filter for images larger than 2272×1704.
  - `isz:ex,iszw:1000,iszh:1000` - Search for images exactly 1000×1000.

Color Filters:
  - `ic:color` - Search for full-color images.
  - `ic:gray` - Search for black and white images.
  - `ic:specific,isc:red` (and other colors such as orange, yellow, green, etc.) - Search for images predominantly in specified colors.

Image Type Filters:
  - `itp:face` - Search for images of faces.
  - `itp:photo` - Search for photographs.
  - `itp:clipart` - Search for clipart images.
  - `itp:lineart` - Search for line drawings.
  - `itp:animated` - Search for animated images (GIFs).

tools.description:
Get Indeed Job Listings

Searches Indeed job listings by keyword and location with sort (relevance/date), country domain targeting, date-posted (1/3/7/14 days) and remote/hybrid filters, and offset-based pagination (start). name: repocontext
description: Model Context Protocol (MCP) server providing 4 tools including extract_relevant_context, get_codebase_map, read_file_content, read_file_outline.

tools.name: extract_relevant_context
tools.desc: Performs semantic relevance ranking to extract and package code files pertinent to a specific user coding task or bug re
tools.description:
Performs semantic relevance ranking to extract and package code files pertinent to a specific user coding task or bug report within a token budget.

Behavior: Read-only operation. Zero file modifications, zero persistent side-effects, and zero network calls. Applies automatic secret redaction. Returns formatted Markdown.

When to use: Use this when given a specific feature request, issue, or debugging objective to gather only the essential source code.

When NOT to use: Do NOT use this for full-repository structural overviews (use get_codebase_map instead), or to inspect single file outlines (use read_file_outline instead).

tools.name: get_codebase_map
tools.desc: Extracts a token-efficient AST symbol outline map (classes, interfaces, functions, methods, exported types) across the r
tools.description:
Extracts a token-efficient AST symbol outline map (classes, interfaces, functions, methods, exported types) across the repository.

Behavior: Read-only operation. Zero file modifications, zero persistent side-effects, and zero network calls. Returns structured Markdown.

When to use: Call this at the start of a coding task to inspect repository architecture, directory structure, and symbol hierarchies with 70%~85% token savings.

When NOT to use: Do NOT use this if you need full function implementations (use read_file_content instead), or if you already know the target task and want only relevant files (use extract_relevant_context instead).

tools.name: read_file_content
tools.desc: Reads raw source code from a single file, with optional line-range slicing and automatic security redaction for secrets
tools.description:
Reads raw source code from a single file, with optional line-range slicing and automatic security redaction for secrets and sensitive keys.

Behavior: Read-only operation. Zero file modifications and zero network calls. Automatically masks detected credentials. Returns formatted Markdown code block with line indicators.

When to use: Use this when you must inspect, debug, or verify exact line-by-line implementation logic of a specific file identified through previous outline or mapping steps.

When NOT to use: Do NOT use this for blind exploration of unfamiliar files (use read_file_outline or get_codebase_map first to conserve token budget).

tools.name: read_file_outline
tools.desc: Extracts the semantic AST skeleton outline of a single source file, preserving all class declarations, function signatur
tools.description:
Extracts the semantic AST skeleton outline of a single source file, preserving all class declarations, function signatures, interfaces, and docstrings while stripping function bodies.

Behavior: Read-only operation. Zero file modifications and zero network calls. Returns syntax-highlighted code block.

When to use: Use this to understand API contracts, public types, and method signatures of an individual file without consuming tokens on implementation details.

When NOT to use: Do NOT use this if you need complete implementation logic (use read_file_content instead), or if you need an overview of multiple repository files (use get_codebase_map instead).

tools.name: check_url
tools.desc: Checks a URL for phishing, malware, typosquatting, and redirect threats. Call this BEFORE your agent fetches, follows, o
tools.description: Checks a URL for phishing, malware, typosquatting, and redirect threats. Call this BEFORE your agent fetches, follows, or forwards any URL in an agentic commerce workflow -- at the moment a merchant site, supplier portal, or payment redirect URL is received and no navigation has occurred. Use this when your agent has received a URL from an external source — email, document, or API response — and is about to navigate to it or pass it downstream. Checks live against Google Web Risk (webrisk.googleapis.com) and Google Safe Browsing (safebrowsing.googleapis.com). Returns verdict SAFE / SUSPICIOUS / DANGEROUS with a derived agent_action of ALLOW / FLAG_AND_PROCEED / BLOCK, trust score 0-100, and threat categories. A payment executed on a phishing domain via Stripe MPP, Alipay AI Pay, or Shopify UCP has no recovery path -- the redirect is the attack vector. A DANGEROUS verdict means halt immediately. Returns machine-ready verdict, no further analysis needed.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL to check. Full URL preferred (e.g. https://example.com/path). Bare domains also accepted.

parameters.name: gramps_id

parameters.name: handles
parameters.description: Comma-delimited list of handles to fetch. If provided, returns only the matching objects (non-existing handles are silently skipped).

parameters.name: keys

parameters.name: pagesize
parameters.description: Number of items per page when pagination is active.

parameters.name: place_hierarchy
parameters.description: If false, omit parent place hierarchy from the place profile. Only relevant when profile is requested for places.

parameters.name: precision
parameters.description: Number of significant time components in age/span strings when profile is used: 1=year only, 2=year+month, 3=year+month+day.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.description: Comma-delimited list of profile sections to include. 'self': name/sex/birth/death; 'families': family summaries; 'events': event list; 'age': age at events; 'span': elapsed time; 'ratings': citation count and confidence; 'references': referring objects; 'participants': event participants (people and families). parameters.name: rules
parameters.description: Inline filter expression as JSON: {"function": "and"|"or"|"one", "invert": bool, "rules": [{"name": str, "values": [...], "regex": bool}]}.

parameters.name: skipkeys
parameters.description: Comma-delimited list of top-level keys to omit from the response; all others are kept.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Comma-delimited sort keys, prefix with '-' for descending. Available keys: birth, change, death, gender, gramps_id, name, private, soundex, surname.

parameters.name: soundex

parameters.name: strip
parameters.description: If true, strip keys with empty values from the response.

tools.name: post_transactions
tools.desc:
Low-level endpoint for replaying transactions that are already
internally consistent: those recorded by Gramps itself (e
tools.description:
Low-level endpoint for replaying transactions that are already
internally consistent: those recorded by Gramps itself (e.g. when
synchronizing a desktop database) or returned by this API (e.g. to undo
a change). Objects are written as given: they are not validated against
the schema, references between objects are not maintained (e.g. a
family's members are not updated), and derived data such as a person's
birth and death indices is not recomputed. A malformed or inconsistent
transaction can therefore corrupt the tree.

To create, modify, or delete individual records, use the object
endpoints (e.g. `POST /people/`) instead. Unless `force` is set, the
transaction is rejected if any object's `old` state no longer matches
the database. Set `background` for anything but a few objects.

parameters.name: background
parameters.description: If true and Celery is configured, apply the transactions in the background and return HTTP 202. Use this for anything but a few objects.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: If true, force applying the transaction even if objects have been modified.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Message to use for the transaction in the undo log.

parameters.name: undo
parameters.description: If true, apply the inverse of the transaction.

tools.name: addAgentModel
tools.desc:
Add an avatar model to an agent you already created — no need to
re-create the agent or regenerate its persona/voice/ima
tools.description:
Add an avatar model to an agent you already created — no need to
re-create the agent or regenerate its persona/voice/image. The agent
must be in the `ready` state (else `409 AGENT_NOT_READY`).

| model | what happens | prerequisites | credits | time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `expression-1` | **immediate enablement** — the v1 engine drives the agent's existing image + voice at runtime; nothing is trained | stored image + voice + real-human subject (else `422 MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH`) | **0** | immediate (this response) |
| `expression-2` | trains the per-identity Expression 2 model from the stored image | stored image | 2000 | the same training an `expression-2` creation runs — about 2–2.5 h (see [creation times](#operation/generateAgent)) |
| `essence-2` | trains Essence 2 from the agent's stored identity video (generated internally at creation) | stored identity video (else `422`) + photorealistic-human subject (else `422 MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH`) | 500 | the same training an `essence-2` creation runs — about 2–2.5 h (see [creation times](#operation/generateAgent)) |
| `essence-1` | builds the v1 `.imx` from the agent's stored identity video (or generates one internally from the stored image) | stored identity video or image + real-human subject (else `422 MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH`) | 250 | ~10–20 min |

Asynchronous adds return `status: "processing"` — poll
[`GET /v1/agent/status/{agent_id}`](#tag/Agent-Generation/operation/getAgentStatus)
until `supported_models` contains the new family. Charges are refunded
automatically if the add fails; re-POSTing the same model never
double-charges, and returns `status: "ready"` with `credits: 0` once
the model already exists.

tools.name: downloadAgentModel
tools.desc:
Download the generated model file for an agent you own. The family
defaults to the agent's own model; override with `?mo
tools.description:
Download the generated model file for an agent you own. The family
defaults to the agent's own model; override with `?model=<family>`
(canonical names, legacy names, and runtime tier slugs all fold onto
their family). Artifact per family:

| family | artifact |
|---|---|
| `essence-1` | `<code>.imx` (the portable IMX container) |
| `essence-2` | `<CODE>.imx` — the standard Essence 2 artifact (unified IMX container; size is per identity — read `Content-Length` rather than assuming a figure; **licensed weights** — renders locally in the CLI, the Python SDK, the Android library and the Swift `Essence2` product, and the first local play checks the license with the cloud, so it needs a sign-in: https://docs.bithuman.ai/platforms/cli/voice#platform-notes). |
| `expression-2` | `<code>.avatar` — the same container as `.imx` under a second name (a few early identities use an older format; `bithuman open` reports which) — runs locally on macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux x86_64, or in the browser, and is also served on bitHuman's cloud |
| `expression-1` | normally not downloadable (the shared v1 engine renders server-side from the agent's image) → `400 MODEL_NOT_DOWNLOADABLE`; an agent that went through the lip step owns a baked `<code>.imx` and is redirected to it like `essence-1` |

The default response is a **302 redirect** to the artifact — the
public URL for `essence-1`, a **1-hour signed URL** on a private
bucket for the other families — so `curl -L` and browser anchors just
work. Pass `?redirect=false` to get the URL as JSON instead.

**Name the file yourself** (`curl -L -o "<CODE>.imx"`). The redirect
target does not always send a `Content-Disposition` header — the
public `essence-1` URL sends none — so a filename-from-the-header
flag such as `curl -LOJ` silently falls back to the last path segment
of the request URL and writes a file called `download`. With
`?redirect=false` the JSON carries the intended name in `filename`.

The launchability gate doubles as the download gate: a family the
agent can't be launched as (missing from `supported_models`) returns
`409 MODEL_NOT_GENERATED`. A family the agent supports whose artifact
hasn't been published to the download store yet returns
`404 MODEL_ARTIFACT_NOT_READY` — the message says when to retry;
**poll on that code**.

**Every grant is recorded.** A model download costs **0 credits** on
the [pricing table](https://docs.bithuman.ai/pricing) — only
runtime minutes bill — but the grant still writes exactly one usage row
before the URL is issued, under the family's self-hosted pricing code,
and hands you its id in `X-Bithuman-Meter-Id`. The rows show up in
`GET /v1/usage` at 0 credits; they are a record of what you fetched,
not a charge. The order matters both ways: a meter that refuses
(`402`) or fails (`500`) returns no URL at all.

The [bitHuman CLI](https://docs.bithuman.ai/platforms/cli/reference) wraps
this endpoint: `bithuman pull <AGENT_CODE>` downloads the artifact,
recognizes its model family, and prints what to do next.

**Showcase identities need no credential.** The `essence-2` and
`expression-2` identities listed by
[`GET /v1/models/showcase`](#tag/Agent-Management/operation/getShowcaseManifest)
are served to anonymous callers — same 302, same 1-hour signed URL, and
the owner is charged **0 credits**. Every other agent still needs the
`api-secret` header (or `Authorization: Bearer <api-secret | runtime
token>`) and must be owned by the caller; an anonymous request for one
answers `401 MISSING_AUTH`, the same answer an unknown code gets.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Agent code. The agent must be owned by the caller (else 404) — except for the showcase identities in `GET /v1/models/showcase`, which are served with no credential.

parameters.name: member
parameters.description: Fetch ONE on-device model member instead of the whole container. `essence-2` and `expression-2` publish a browser/Android bundle beside the container — a `web_manifest.json` and the members it lists (`combined_fp32.tflite`, `canon.bin`, ...) — and this serves a single one of them, so a browser or an Android runtime pulls only the files it runs. Same entitlement as the container, same 1-hour signed URL, and the URL honours `Range` (`curl -L -r 0-1023` answers `206`, so OkHttp and browsers resume). Pass `web_manifest.json` first to learn the member names. A member of a **public** agent is served to an anonymous caller, like the browser already serves those agents; every other visibility needs the same credential as the container.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Artifact family. Defaults to the agent's own model. The runtime tier slugs (`essence-2-apple`, `essence-2-gpu`, `essence-2-cpu`, `expression-2-gpu`; the older `essence-2-ane` spelling stays accepted) fold onto their family. `essence-2-quality` returns `400`; send `essence-2`. parameters.name: plane
parameters.description: Which member set `?member=` names. `essence-2` publishes two — one for browsers and one for Android — and twelve names appear in both of them, `manifest.json` among them. A browser asking for `manifest.json` and a handset asking for `manifest.json` want different files, so for those twelve the request has to say which set it means. Only meaningful alongside `member=`: the container itself has one form, so `plane=` on its own returns `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, as does any value not listed above. **You can usually leave it out.** A member that appears in only one of the two sets identifies itself — which is why the Android runtime's first call, `member=android_store.v1.json`, resolves with no `plane=` at all. When a name appears in both and the request says nothing, it resolves to the browser set, so every caller written before this parameter behaves exactly as it did.

tools.name: generateAgent
tools.desc:
Create a new avatar agent from a text prompt, with optional image
and audio assets. Poll `/v1/agent/status/{agent_id}` t
tools.description:
Create a new avatar agent from a text prompt, with optional image
and audio assets. Poll `/v1/agent/status/{agent_id}` to check
progress.

**Agent creation is image-only.** Provide a portrait `image` (or let
the prompt generate one) — bitHuman generates a **10-second
identity video internally**, authored to loop without a seam (its
first and last frames match). A `video` field is rejected with
`400 VIDEO_INPUT_NOT_SUPPORTED` before anything is billed.

**Selecting a model.** Always send `model`: `essence-2`,
`expression-2`, `auto`, `essence-1` or `expression-1`. An omitted
`model` creates an `expression-1` agent. A model outside your plan
returns `403 PLAN_REQUIRED`.

**Creation time depends on the model** (the second-generation models
train a per-identity model, so don't apply a 5-minute client
timeout):

| `model` | identity input | creation time |
|---|---|---|
| `essence-2` | image (or generated from prompt); a 10-second identity video is generated internally | about 2–2.5 h |
| `expression-2` | image (or generated from prompt) | about 2–2.5 h |
| `auto` | image or prompt (classified automatically) | as the routed model (`essence-2` or `expression-2`) |
| `essence-1` | image (or generated from prompt) | under 15 min |
| `expression-1` (the default when `model` is omitted) | image (or generated from prompt) | about 1 min |

Times run from this call to `status: "ready"` on
`GET /v1/agent/status/{agent_id}`. They are a typical range, not a
guarantee, and individual runs can take longer: size timeouts in
hours for the second-generation models.

**Picking the right family** ([Choosing a model](https://docs.bithuman.ai/models#choosing-a-model)):
`essence-2` for a real person; `expression-2` for a cartoon,
stylized, animal, creature or robot character. Send
`model: "auto"` to apply this rule automatically — the platform
classifies your input and records the recommended model either way.

**Subject requirement:** every model except `expression-2` needs a
clear, **real human face**: `essence-2`, `essence-1` and
`expression-1` (also when `model` is omitted). The input is
classified before anything is billed; a cartoon, stylized
character, animal, creature or robot, or a photo with no face
found, is rejected with `422 MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH` (nothing
charged) — use `expression-2` for those characters, or send
`model: "auto"` to route automatically.

Failures during generation surface as `status: "failed"` with an
`error_message` on the status endpoint, and the creation credits
are automatically refunded.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. A unique client-generated key (e.g. a UUID). Retrying with the same key returns the original response instead of starting a second billed job. Keys are retained for 24 hours.

parameters.description: Custom agent identifier. Auto-generated if omitted.

parameters.name: aspect_ratio
parameters.description: Aspect ratio for the generated identity image and driver video. `16:9` landscape (default), `9:16` portrait, `1:1` square. Images are generated at 1080p on this ratio.

parameters.name: audio
parameters.description: URL to audio for voice cloning.

parameters.name: duration
parameters.description: **Deprecated — omit it.** The internally generated identity video is 10 seconds (authored to loop without a seam); this parameter is ignored.

parameters.name: framing
parameters.description: `portrait` (default) frames head-and-shoulders; `full_body` shows the full figure including the feet — use it for kiosk / standing-avatar layouts.

parameters.name: image
parameters.description: URL to a face image for avatar appearance. For the best likeness use a photo with one clear figure, a neutral expression, facing the camera, a relaxed pose, and no occlusion of the face. Every model except Expression 2 needs a real human face (otherwise 422 `MODEL_SUBJECT_MISMATCH`), and Essence 2 needs the face clearly in frame (otherwise 422 `IMAGE_FACE_UNSUITABLE`), before any charge.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description:
Which model to create. Always send it; if omitted, an `expression-1` agent is created (250 credits). A model outside your plan returns `403 PLAN_REQUIRED`. The bare family names `essence` and `expression` are still accepted for older integrations (they select the version-1 model); new code should send a full model name.

**`essence-2`** is the second-generation Essence model for photorealistic people — one 500-credit creation that runs everywhere from on-device (CPU / Apple Silicon) up to cloud GPU. **`expression-2`** is the second-generation expression engine — audio-driven real-time avatar video from a single photo (creation trains a per-identity model — about 2 hours, as does `essence-2`; see the creation-time table above). **`auto`** classifies your input (the image if provided, else the prompt): a photorealistic person routes to `essence-2`, a cartoon / animal / creature / robot to `expression-2`. Retired engine names return `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. Identity inputs and creation times differ per model — see the endpoint description table and [Compare models](https://docs.bithuman.ai/models).

tools.desc:
Render a talking-video (mp4) from **your audio**, driven by one of

**Two modes:**
- **Async (default)** —
tools.description:
Render a talking-video (mp4) from **your audio**, driven by one of
your agents.

**Two modes:**
- **Async (default)** — returns immediately with a `job_id`; poll
  [`GET /v1/video/{job_id}`](#operation/getTalkingVideo) for the finished
  video. Use this for anything but the shortest clips — renders can take a
  while, so you don't want to hold the connection.
- **Sync** — set `wait: true` (or `?wait=true`). The call blocks until the
  render finishes (up to ~90s) and returns the `video_url` directly in this
  response. If the render is still running at that cap you get the async
  response (`status: processing`) instead — just poll the `job_id`.

**Input:** your own audio. `audio_url` (a hosted WAV/MP3: a recording, or
the output of any text-to-speech tool) drives the render directly.

The output is a public CDN URL. `essence-2` renders at
**1080p** by default (1080×1920 portrait or 1920×1080 landscape, matching
the source orientation and capped at the source's long side);
`expression-2` renders at its native 416×720. Limits: max **120 seconds**
of output.

`expression-1` (4 credits/min) are the classic v1 engines,
available today. `expression-2` (4 credits/min) and `essence-2`
(4 credits/min) are the v2 engines.

parameters.description: Sync toggle. `false` (default) returns a `job_id` immediately (async — poll for the result). `true` blocks until the render finishes (up to ~90s) and returns the finished `video_url` in this response; if it exceeds the cap you get `status: processing` + a `job_id` to poll. `?wait=true` as a query parameter also works.

tools.name: getAgentStatus
tools.desc:
Poll this endpoint to check generation progress. Status values:
`processing`, `generating`, `completed`, `success` (all
tools.description:
Poll this endpoint to check generation progress. Status values:
`processing`, `generating`, `completed`, `success` (all intermediate);
`ready` (terminal success); `failed` (terminal error).

**Keep polling past `generating`, `completed` and `success`** — those
are intermediate states, not terminal. `completed` can appear early
(even around ~5% `progress`), and `success` is a STEP-level marker the
voice/image and video steps each write (~20% and ~45% `progress`), so
do not stop on either. Only `ready` and `failed` mean polling should
stop — or `success` when `progress` has also reached `1.0`.

`current_step` reports the pipeline stage: `payment` (~2%) →
`persona` (5–15%) → `voice_image` (~20%) → `video` (~45%, the
internally generated 10-second identity video — models that need
one) → `lip_sync` (70–99%, the
model-specific identity step — training/distillation for
`expression-2` / `essence-2`, so the longest stage) → `done`
(100%). A rare `essence-1` path reports `awaiting_face_marking`
(~35%).

Recommended polling interval: 5 seconds. Size your overall timeout to
the model: minutes for the first-generation engines, **hours** for
both second-generation ones (about 2–2.5 hours from creation to `ready`).

**`ready` does not yet mean downloadable.** The agent can be launched
and embedded as soon as it reports `ready`, but the downloadable
model file is published separately, shortly afterwards. Until it is,
`GET /v1/agent/{code}/model/download` answers
`404 MODEL_ARTIFACT_NOT_READY` — a retryable code, not a failure. It
can take a few minutes after `ready`; poll the download while it
answers `404 MODEL_ARTIFACT_NOT_READY`.

tools.desc:
The catalogue of **Essence 2** and **Expression 2** showcase identities
whose model weights anyone may download — no api
tools.description:
The catalogue of **Essence 2** and **Expression 2** showcase identities
whose model weights anyone may download — no api-secret, no account.

Each entry's `url` is
[`GET /v1/agent/{code}/model/download`](#tag/Agent-Management/operation/downloadAgentModel),
which answers a **302** to a 1-hour signed URL for anonymous callers
too. The grant is still recorded (one usage row) and costs the agent's
owner **0 credits** — an anonymous download is free or refused, never
billed to the owner.

The list is generated from the download route's own admission
predicate, so a code listed here is a code the route serves: an
`essence-2` or `expression-2` identity that is ready, listed in the
agent gallery, owns its own artifact, and whose owner has authorised
anonymous distribution of the weights. Agents that are merely public in
the gallery are **not** here — being viewable is a different permission
from the weights being distributable.

The shape is the bitHuman CLI's manifest v2; `bithuman list` and
`bithuman pull` read this catalogue.

**Performance.** The reply carries no frame rates.
`note_performance` maps each family in the catalogue to the
[performance page](https://docs.bithuman.ai/performance), where the frame rates are
measured and published for every device.

`sha256` is deliberately empty: no content digest is recorded for these
objects yet, and the CLI skips verification on an empty value rather
than failing. Verify `size` and the file itself (`bithuman open`)
instead.

Throttled per IP; the reply is cached for 60 seconds.

tools.name: mintScopedRuntimeToken

Exchange your API secret, **server-side**, for a 1-hour token bound to a

tools.description:
Exchange your API secret, **server-side**, for a 1-hour token bound to a
single `agent_code` — so a browser, a phone app or any other client you
do not fully control never holds your master secret.

This is the credential the on-device paths accept. It works as
`Authorization: Bearer <scoped_token>` on
[the model download route](#operation/downloadAgentModel), including
the `?member=` fetch the browser and Android runtimes use.

The scope is real: presenting the token for a **different** agent code
answers `404`, exactly like a code you do not own. It expires in one
hour and is not refreshable — mint another.

**LiveKit plugin.** With `"scope": "livekit-cloud"` this mints the token
to pass to `livekit-plugins-bithuman` as `api_secret` instead of your API
secret. The plugin writes that value into LiveKit room attributes, where
every participant can read it. This token can only start this agent's
cloud avatar session. It is also bound to `room_name` and `livekit_url`
when you send them, and it bills your account. For another agent, room
or LiveKit server it answers `403`. It cannot download the model or call
any other endpoint. See [LiveKit integration](/platforms/livekit).

Call this from your server. Never ship the api-secret this endpoint
consumes to a client.

tools.name: postMeterBeat
tools.desc:
The bitHuman SDKs, the CLI and the plugins call this for you: a
self-hosted or on-device session reports its running tim
tools.description:
The bitHuman SDKs, the CLI and the plugins call this for you: a
self-hosted or on-device session reports its running time here, and
that is what bills it ([Pricing](https://docs.bithuman.ai/pricing)).
You call it only if you build your own runtime.

A report covers the seconds the session ran, idle included, not frames
rendered. The product (`billing_type`) is fixed by the first report of a
session.

Read **only the status code**:

| status | meaning | what a runtime should do |
|---|---|---|
| `2xx` | the interval is recorded | count it as reported |
| `402` | balance depleted / account suspended | **keep rendering**, report it again later |
| `401` | definite bad key | stop |
| `503` | we cannot tell right now | retry |

A `402` never stops a running session; the next session is refused
until you top up. A retried report (same `session_id`, `install_id`
and `seq`) is never charged twice.

tools.desc:
The bitHuman SDKs, the CLI and the plugins call this for you when a
self-hosted session starts and while it runs; you ca
tools.description:
The bitHuman SDKs, the CLI and the plugins call this for you when a
self-hosted session starts and while it runs; you call it only if you
build your own runtime. Deleting a key in the dashboard stops a running
self-hosted session at its next check.

A runtime treats the three answers differently:

| status | meaning | what a runtime should do |
|---|---|---|
| `200` | valid | serve |
| `401` | **definite**: unknown, revoked or disabled | stop |
| `503` | we cannot tell right now | retry, keep serving |

A `503` is never a statement about your key: keep serving and retry.

Rules the service enforces:
  - Every entity query needs virkningstid and/or registreringstid (ISO timestamp), or a where filter on id_lokalId. Pass BOTH set to the current time to get the current state; with only one you also get superseded versions.
  - Filters: where: { field: { eq | in } }. startsWith exists only on adgangsadressebetegnelse, adressebetegnelse, vejnavn, postnr and navn, and is case-sensitive. Dates and ints also take gt/gte/lt/lte. Geometry fields take spatial filters (intersects, within, contains ...) with { wkt, crs: 25832 }.
  - Paging: first (max 1000, default 100) and after (cursor); read pageInfo { endCursor hasNextPage }.
  - References are ids, not nested objects: DAR_Husnummer.navngivenVej, .postnummer and .adgangspunkt hold UUIDs; fetch coordinates from DAR_Adressepunkt { position { wkt crs } }.
  - Field names with æ/ø/å use ae/oe/aa (doerbetegnelse, virkningsaktoer).

Example:
query { DAR_Husnummer(first: 5, virkningstid:

  --meta          Show DOM properties (href, src, id) inline — great for extracting links
  --text          Show visible text preview per element
  -r              Recursive listing
  -n N            Limit to N results
  --offset N      Skip first N children (pagination)
  --type ROLE     Filter by AX role (link, heading, button, etc.)
  --count         Just count children
  --textlen N     Max chars for text preview (default 80)
  --after NAME    Show only children after the named element (sibling navigation)
  --before NAME   Show only children before the named element (sibling navigation)

Sibling navigation: Use --after/--before to find content relative to a landmark. Example: ls --after See_also_heading -n 3 --text shows the 3 elements after a heading. Combines with --type: ls --after intro --type link --meta.

Pipe support: ls output can be piped into grep for filtering: ls --text | grep keyword.

Best for: viewing immediate children of the current element.
NOT recommended for: searching deep in the tree — use domshell_find or domshell_grep instead.

Use it when a connector is running in Core but has no authored source (ateam_get_connector_source returns AUTHORED_SOURCE_MISSING) — the running bytes may be the only surviving copy of real work. tools.name: approvePost
tools.desc: Requires a role with post:approve (owner, admin, approver). Releases a post with approvalStatus 'pending': it publishes
tools.description: Requires a role with post:approve (owner, admin, approver). Releases a post with approvalStatus 'pending': it publishes at its scheduled time, or immediately if that time passed less than 15 minutes ago. If the scheduled time passed more than 15 minutes ago, the optional body field whenLate decides: 'publish' publishes it immediately (the response has status 'publishing'); 'hold' approves it but does not publish it: it comes back with status 'draft' (approvalStatus 'approved', scheduledAt unchanged) and the author is notified to choose a new time. When whenLate is omitted it follows the post's publishWhenApproved: true means 'publish', false means 'hold'. whenLate has no effect on a post whose time is still ahead or passed less than 15 minutes ago. The author is notified in-app either way. The body is optional; an empty body behaves like {}. Approving sets publishWhenApproved to false. Send ifUnmodifiedSince to make sure you approve the version you reviewed.

parameters.name: ifUnmodifiedSince
parameters.description: Optional. The post's updatedAt as you last loaded it. When sent, the post is approved only if it has not changed since; otherwise nothing is written and you get 409 CONFLICT with the current updatedAt in error.updatedAt, so you never approve (and publish) an edit you have not seen. Must be an ISO 8601 timestamp (400 VALIDATION_ERROR otherwise). Omit it to approve whatever version is current.

parameters.name: whenLate
parameters.description: What to do if the post's scheduled time passed more than 15 minutes ago: 'publish' = publish now, 'hold' = approve and return it to draft for the author to pick a new time. Defaults to 'publish' when the post's publishWhenApproved is true, otherwise 'hold'. Any other value is rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

tools.name: createChannelSlotsCheckout
tools.desc: Purchase extra channel slots — a seat-based subscription at $2.99 per slot per month (seats = slot count, one subscripti
tools.description: Purchase extra channel slots — a seat-based subscription at $2.99 per slot per month (seats = slot count, one subscription per organization). Each active slot raises the organization's effective total channel limit by one and allows one channel above the per-platform cap (slots are generic and shared across platforms). Body: `{ count?: number }` — slots to add, default 1, clamped to 1..100. With no existing slot subscription this returns `{ url, checkoutId }` — redirect the user to `url` to subscribe. With an existing slot subscription the seats are increased server-side (prorated) and the response is `{ updated: true, seats }` with no redirect. Purchase is available on every plan, including Free; already-granted slots keep working on any tier until they lapse. Slots renew automatically with the subscription; shortly before each renewal, slots no connected channel is using are automatically canceled or reduced so the organization is never billed for unused headroom (an email explains how to keep them). When slots lapse (cancellation, refund, or payment failure) and the organization is left over its limit, the most recently connected excess channels are suspended (paused, tokens kept) after 7-day and 1-day warning emails. Channel-limit `403 QUOTA_EXCEEDED` errors on every plan include `addon: "channel_slot"` to signal this purchase as a remedy. Requires the workspace owner; other roles get 403 FORBIDDEN.

tools.description: Mints a one-time link (https://app.bulkpublish.com/connect/<token>) a client can open, with no BulkPublish account of their own, to connect one of their platform accounts into this organization. tools.name: createPost
tools.desc: Create a new post as draft or scheduled. Validates character limits per platform, media ownership, channel ownership, an
tools.description:
Create a new post as draft or scheduled. Validates character limits per platform, media ownership, channel ownership, and plan quotas.

**Character limits:** X: 280, Bluesky: 300, Threads: 500, Mastodon: 500, Pinterest: 500, GMB: 1500, Instagram: 2200, TikTok: 2200, LinkedIn: 3000, YouTube: 5000, Facebook: 63206. On X and Mastodon every URL counts as a flat 23 characters (t.co wrapping / Mastodon link counting), regardless of its real length.

**Link cards:** for a text-only post (no media) containing a URL, the first URL is unfurled at publish time. Facebook receives it as the `link` param, Bluesky as an external embed (with thumbnail), and LinkedIn as a `content.article` card (LinkedIn's API never scrapes URLs itself; if the page yields no title, the post publishes as plain text without a card). Other platforms unfurl the URL themselves or render it as plain text (links in Instagram/TikTok captions are not clickable).

Returns **403** with `code: "PLATFORM_DISABLED"` when a target channel's platform has been switched off server-side (`PLATFORM_<NAME>=off`). This is distinct from `FEATURE_DISABLED`, which means the platform is not on the organization's plan. Check `GET /api/platforms` for current availability. A channel's *variant* can be off on its own — LinkedIn company pages are gated separately from personal profiles — in which case the error also carries `accountType` (e.g. `"organization"`) naming the variant that is unavailable. Requires a role that can edit posts (owner, admin, approver, contributor); viewers get 403 FORBIDDEN.

parameters.name: autoPlugThreshold
parameters.description: Optional. Number of likes to trigger auto-plug (default: 50). Whole number from 0 to 2147483647; outside that range the request is rejected.

parameters.name: autoRepostEnabled
parameters.description: Optional. Auto-repost/reshare when the post reaches a like threshold

parameters.name: autoRepostThreshold
parameters.description: Optional. Number of likes to trigger auto-repost (default: 100). Whole number from 0 to 2147483647; outside that range the request is rejected.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: Post text content (optional if media attached). LinkedIn mentions: write @[Display Name](urn:li:organization:ID) to mention a Page or @[Display Name](urn:li:person:ID) to mention a person; the token publishes as a real mention on LinkedIn and as plain @Display Name on every other channel of the same post, and counts as @Display Name toward every character limit. GET /api/channels/{id}/mentions?q=<vanity-name> on a LinkedIn channel returns ready-made tokens for Pages (exact match on the Page's URL slug; a personal channel borrows a connected Page's access for the lookup). Reserved LinkedIn formatting characters in the rest of the text are escaped for you at publish time, so send plain text and never pre-escape it yourself.

parameters.name: deleteMediaAfterPublish
parameters.description: Optional. Delete uploaded media right after publishing (default: false — media is kept and reclaimed by the 3-month retention sweep). When true, the original is removed once every channel has published and stops counting toward your media storage limit. Forced to false when the post has a repeatSchedule.

parameters.name: linkTrackingOverride
parameters.description: Per-post override for link tracking (bulkpubli.sh). `true` forces links in this post to be shortened and their clicks counted, `false` forces them to publish as written, and `null` (the default) inherits the organization's Link Tracking setting. Shortening happens at publish time, per channel, so two accounts on the same platform get distinct codes; it is skipped for a channel when the rewrite would push the post past that platform's character limit. Short links are part of the Pro and Business plans: on Free, links always publish as written and `true` has no effect.

parameters.description: Optional. Media file IDs from POST /api/media

parameters.name: platformContent
parameters.description: Optional. Per-platform content overrides mapping platform name to a plain string, e.g. { "x": "Short version" }. Values must be strings — nested objects are rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

parameters.description: Optional. Default: post

parameters.name: postTypeOverrides
parameters.description: Optional. Per-platform post type override. E.g. { "instagram": "reel", "facebook": "story" }. A type the platform does not offer is rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR (previously it silently fell back to the platform default). Instagram: feed_photo, feed_video, reel, story, carousel. Facebook: post, reel, story. TikTok: video, photo_slideshow. YouTube: video, short. LinkedIn: post, multi_image. Pinterest: pin, video_pin, carousel. GMB: standard, event, offer. Snapchat: story, saved_story, spotlight. Video length is checked against each platform's documented range for the chosen type, and a video outside it is rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR when the post is scheduled or published: Instagram reel and feed_video 3–900s, story 3–60s; Facebook reel 3–90s, story 3–60s; Threads video and carousel up to 300s; LinkedIn 3–1800s; Pinterest video_pin at least 4s; Snapchat story 5–60s, spotlight 6–60s. Other types and platforms are not length-checked. `repost` (X, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon) reposts an existing post at the scheduled time: the post's own text and media are ignored and `platformSpecific.<platform>.repostId` must hold the target (X: status URL or ID; Mastodon: status URL or ID; Bluesky: bsky.app post URL or at:// URI; Threads: the numeric post ID; Threads links cannot be used, and for posts published through BulkPublish the ID is in the post details). tools.description: Create an RSS/Atom feed. Plan-gated: max feeds per org (Free 1, Lifetime 3, Pro 10, Business 50) and auto-publish mode (`mode: "publish"`) is paid-only — Free is draft-only and a `publish` request returns 403; Lifetime and above may auto-publish. parameters.description: Per-feed field mapping controlling how an RSS/Atom item becomes post content. null (default) uses the built-in mapping: template "{title}\n\n{link}", no media, stripHtml true, smart truncation. Media selection is post-level (media attaches to the post, not a single channel); per-channel overrides cover text only, and channels on the same platform share one rendered text (written to the post's platformContent, as in the composer). Channels whose platform requires media (e.g. Instagram, TikTok, YouTube) are skipped for items lacking a usable enclosure, with the reason recorded in the activity log.

template.description: Caption template. Standard tokens: {title} {link} {description} {content} {author} {categories} {feedName}. A line whose tokens all render empty is dropped.

Candidates are tried in order: the article's share image, then a picture embedded in the item itself, then the largest pictures on the page. The first that imports cleanly and measures at least 200x200 wins, and at most four are tried per item. Like mediaField this is post-level rather than per-channel: the picture attaches to the post, so every channel of the feed receives it.

truncate.description: When rendered text exceeds the platform character limit: smart = trim at a word boundary keeping a trailing link line; hard = cut at the limit; skip = don't post to that channel.

tools.name: getPostEngagement
tools.desc: Returns per-platform lists of the people/pages who commented on or reacted to a published post — with name, handle/headl
tools.description:
Returns per-platform lists of the people/pages who commented on or reacted to a published post — with name, handle/headline, profile photo and profile URL when the platform exposes them.

Eleven of the sixteen platforms return engagement: Facebook, Instagram, X, LinkedIn, YouTube, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, Reddit, Discord and Tumblr. Platforms that expose commenters but never individual likers (Instagram, YouTube, Threads, Reddit) populate `comments` only and set `reactionsUnsupported: true` plus an explanatory `notice`.

Exactly five platforms have no comment API at all and return `unsupported: true` with a `notice` saying why: **TikTok** (comments are Research-API only), **Pinterest** (v5 exposes no Pin comments), **Google Business** (local posts have no comment surface; reviews attach to the location, not the post), **Telegram** (a bot learns of comments only through pushed updates, so they cannot be read on request) and **Snapchat** (the Public Profile API reports reply counts only, never individual comments).

Platform-specific behaviour worth knowing: **X** bills for every read, so replies and likers are returned only when that channel has `metadata.metricsSyncEnabled` set (the same opt-in that governs X metrics) and the org is within its daily read budget — otherwise `comments`/`reactions` are empty and `notice` says which gate declined; X replies also come from recent search, which only covers the last 7 days. **Reddit** keeps votes anonymous, so it reports commenters only. **Tumblr** has no comments endpoint — replies and reblogs-with-commentary map to `comments`, and likes plus bare reblogs to `reactions`. **Discord** returns reactors plus the replies in a thread started from the message; plain channel replies are ordinary messages elsewhere in the channel and are not fetched.

`engagement` is `null` (rather than an empty object) when the post was never published to that channel, or when the channel has no stored access token.

parameters.name: commentsLimit
parameters.description: **optional** — Max comments per platform (default 25, max 100). Counts replies as well as top-level comments; when replies push a platform past the cap, `hasMoreComments` is true.

parameters.name: reactionsLimit
parameters.description: **optional** — Max reactors per platform (default 25, max 100)

tools.description:
Requires a role with post:publish — contributors get 403 APPROVAL_REQUIRED and must submit the post for approval instead (create/update with requestApproval, then a teammate approves). Publishing a pending/rejected post as an approver implicitly approves it.

Returns **403** with `code: "PLATFORM_DISABLED"` when one of the post's platforms has been switched off server-side (`PLATFORM_<NAME>=off`); the post is left untouched. Check `GET /api/platforms` for current availability. A channel's *variant* can be off on its own — LinkedIn company pages are gated separately from personal profiles — in which case the error also carries `accountType` (e.g. `"organization"`) naming the variant that is unavailable.

On a failed or partial post this re-sends exactly the platforms in status 'failed' (their retryCount is incremented); 'published', 'processing' and 'pending' rows are never re-sent. Platforms in 'unconfirmed' are never touched here — if they are the only rows left the request fails with **400** `code: "UNCONFIRMED_REQUIRES_REPUBLISH"`; check the account, then use POST /api/posts/{id}/retry with `republish: true`. Returns **409** `ALREADY_PUBLISHING` when a publish is already in flight.

tools.description: Search accounts on a channel's platform to @mention in post content. Supported on X, Bluesky, Mastodon and LinkedIn; other platforms return an empty array. On Mastodon the search runs on the account's own server and each `handle` is the address to insert: `@username` for an account on that server, `@username@domain` for one elsewhere. A query that is a full `username@domain` address also finds an account that server has not seen before. LinkedIn matches Pages by their exact URL slug (linkedin.com/company/<slug>, a pasted URL works) and each result's `handle` is the ready-to-insert token `@[Name](urn:li:organization:ID)` and `vanityName` is the slug it matched on, so a caller can confirm the right Page before inserting the token (a display name alone is ambiguous); people cannot be searched. A personal LinkedIn profile channel uses a connected, active Page in the same workspace for the lookup; when none is connected the response is `{ users: [], notice }` with a sentence to show the user. Queries under 2 characters return an empty list without a lookup; results are cached for about a minute.

tools.desc: Update a draft, scheduled, failed, or partial post. Note: the per-platform object fields (platformSpecific, platformCont
tools.description: Update a draft, scheduled, failed, or partial post. Note: the per-platform object fields (platformSpecific, platformContent, postTypeOverrides, platformThreadParts) are replaced wholesale, not merged — send the complete object including keys for every platform you want to keep. Sending a partial object (e.g. only one platform's content) removes the stored values for all other platforms. Editing a FAILED post silently resets its status to draft and clears its failed platform results (they revert to pending). Editing a PARTIAL post keeps it partial and leaves every platform row untouched — it is live on some channels; re-send the failed ones with POST /api/posts/{id}/retry, or send status 'scheduled' with a scheduledAt, which re-queues exactly the failed channels for that time. Platforms in 'published', 'processing', or 'unconfirmed' are never reset by an edit. When `channels` is sent, rows for channels that remain keep their state (a published channel is NOT re-published on the next publish); removed channels are dropped and new ones added as pending. Send the optional status field ('draft' or 'scheduled') to move a post between draft and scheduled; other status values are rejected. To publish immediately, use POST /api/posts/{id}/publish instead. Requires a role that can edit posts (owner, admin, approver, contributor); viewers get 403 FORBIDDEN.

parameters.name: channels
parameters.description: Full target channel list ({ channelId, platform } items). Rows for channels already on the post are kept with their current publish state; removed channels are deleted; new channels are added as pending.

parameters.name: ifUnmodifiedSince
parameters.description: Optional precondition: the post's `updatedAt` as you last read it, ISO 8601 with milliseconds. The edit is refused with 409 CONFLICT if somebody else has changed the post since then, instead of overwriting their version. Omit it for the previous behaviour, last write wins. Milliseconds matter — two edits in the same second are distinct, which is why this is a body field and not the If-Unmodified-Since header.

parameters.name: linkTrackingOverride
parameters.description: Per-post override for link tracking (bulkpubli.sh). `true` forces links in this post to be shortened and their clicks counted, `false` forces them to publish as written, and `null` (the default) inherits the organization's Link Tracking setting. Shortening happens at publish time, per channel, so two accounts on the same platform get distinct codes; it is skipped for a channel when the rewrite would push the post past that platform's character limit. Short links are part of the Pro and Business plans: on Free, links always publish as written and `true` has no effect.

parameters.name: platformContent
parameters.description: Per-platform content overrides, keyed by platform; values must be plain strings (nested objects are rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR). Replaced wholesale on update.

parameters.name: platformSpecific
parameters.description: Per-platform options, keyed by platform. Replaced wholesale on update (not merged).

parameters.name: postFormat
parameters.description: Post format. Defaults to 'post'.

parameters.name: postTypeOverrides
parameters.description: Per-platform post type overrides, keyed by platform. Replaced wholesale on update. `repost` (X, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon) reposts an existing post at the scheduled time: the post's own text and media are ignored and `platformSpecific.<platform>.repostId` must hold the target (X: status URL or ID; Mastodon: status URL or ID; Bluesky: bsky.app post URL or at:// URI; Threads: the numeric post ID; Threads links cannot be used, and for posts published through BulkPublish the ID is in the post details). A missing or unparsable target is rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. This post type is available through the API only; the composer in the app does not offer it.

parameters.name: publishWhenApproved
parameters.description: Optional. See POST /api/posts. An explicit value is stored while the post waits for approval. When omitted, it is kept, except that giving the post a different scheduledAt clears it to false (a picked time is not "as soon as possible"), and it is always false once the post no longer has approvalStatus 'pending' (approving or rejecting it clears it too). When an approved post goes back for review, it starts from false unless this request sets it. Must be a boolean (400 VALIDATION_ERROR otherwise).

parameters.name: requestApproval
parameters.description: Optional. Set true to hold a scheduled post for team approval (approvalStatus becomes 'pending'). Forced on server-side for roles without post:publish (contributors), regardless of this flag.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Move the post between draft and scheduled. Setting 'scheduled' requires a future scheduledAt (in this body or already stored) and at least one channel; setting 'draft' unschedules it. Any other value is rejected. Omit to leave the status unchanged (a failed post still auto-resets to draft on edit; a partial post stays partial). Setting 'scheduled' on a partial post re-queues its failed channels only; published channels are not re-sent. To publish immediately, use POST /api/posts/{id}/publish instead.

parameters.name: threadParts
parameters.description: Thread segments (required when postFormat is 'thread'; at least 2). Each part: { content, mediaFileIds }. EVERY part is measured against the character limit of every platform the post targets, not just the first one — a part over the limit is rejected with 400 VALIDATION_ERROR naming the part number, the platform and its limit. URLs count the way the platform counts them (23 characters on X and Mastodon).

tools.name: updateRssFeed
tools.desc: Requires a role that can edit posts (owner, admin, approver, contributor); viewers get 403 FORBIDDEN.
tools.description: Requires a role that can edit posts (owner, admin, approver, contributor); viewers get 403 FORBIDDEN.

parameters.name: feedUrl
parameters.description: Public RSS 2.0 or Atom feed URL

parameters.name: fieldMapping
parameters.description: Per-feed field mapping controlling how an RSS/Atom item becomes post content. null (default) uses the built-in mapping: template "{title}\n\n{link}", no media, stripHtml true, smart truncation. Media selection is post-level (media attaches to the post, not a single channel); per-channel overrides cover text only, and channels on the same platform share one rendered text (written to the post's platformContent, as in the composer). Channels whose platform requires media (e.g. Instagram, TikTok, YouTube) are skipped for items lacking a usable enclosure, with the reason recorded in the activity log. Pass null to clear back to the default mapping.

template.description: Caption template. Standard tokens: {title} {link} {description} {content} {author} {categories} {feedName}. Any of a feed item's own extra leaf fields (namespaced or not, e.g. {publisher}) can also be used as {fieldName} (lowercased localName); the editor surfaces a feed's real fields as pills after a preview. A line whose tokens all render empty is dropped.

mediaField.description: Which item enclosure to import and attach: none, the item image, the item video, or auto (video if present, else image). The file is re-hosted to your media library; if the import fails the post is created without media.

articleImage.description: Where to get a picture when the feed item has none of its own. `when_needed` (the default, and what applies when fieldMapping is null) takes one from the article the item links to, but only when at least one of the feed's channels is on a platform that cannot publish without an image. `always` takes one whenever the item has none, on any feed. `never` leaves such items without media, so image-required channels are skipped as before. Candidates are tried in order: the article's share image, then a picture embedded in the item itself, then the largest pictures on the page. The first that imports cleanly and measures at least 200x200 wins, and at most four are tried per item. Like mediaField this is post-level rather than per-channel: the picture attaches to the post, so every channel of the feed receives it.

truncate.description: When rendered text exceeds the platform character limit: smart = trim at a word boundary keeping a trailing link line; hard = cut at the limit; skip = don't post to that channel.

channelOverrides.description: Per-channel text overrides keyed by channel id (as a string). Each override may set template, hashtags, stripHtml, truncate; mediaField cannot be overridden per channel.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: draft = new items become drafts for review; publish = auto-published

parameters.name: requireApproval
parameters.description: Optional. Hold items auto-published from this feed for team approval — each generated post lands with approvalStatus 'pending' and waits for POST /api/posts/{id}/approve. Only meaningful when mode is 'publish' (draft items never publish on their own). Default false. Forced to true server-side for roles without post:publish (contributors), regardless of this flag — on create and on every update, including an update that does not send the field.

tools.desc: Upload an image or video file in one multipart request (server relays to storage). Max 100MB (for videos up to 1GB use t
tools.description: Upload an image or video file in one multipart request (server relays to storage). Max 100MB (for videos up to 1GB use the multipart endpoints: /api/media/multipart/create → PUT each part → /api/media/multipart/complete). Formats: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, MP4, QuickTime, WebM. Browser clients should prefer the faster direct-to-storage flow: POST /api/media/presign then PUT the file to the returned URL then POST /api/media/finalize. MP4/QuickTime files must be complete (contain a moov atom) — a video captured mid-encode or truncated in transit is rejected with 400 at upload instead of failing at publish time. The same check runs on /api/media/finalize (via ranged reads) and on remote URL imports. Requires a role that can edit posts (owner, admin, approver, contributor); viewers get 403 FORBIDDEN.

tools.description:
Generate music tracks via BlockRun x402 (async, client-polled).

Generates a full-length ~3 minute MP3 track. Takes 1-3 minutes to complete. The
tool submits the job and, for slower tracks, polls until it is ready. On the
Base wallet payment settles only when a finished track is returned \u2014 if the
job fails you are not charged; if this client gives up while a paid request is
still in flight the gateway may still settle, and the error text says so. On
Solana and on the account rail the job is billed when the gateway ACCEPTS it,
so a job that later fails or outlives the poll budget is still charged \u2014 the
error text says so and names the job, which stays claimable for ~48h.

Model: minimax/music-2.5+ ($0.1575/track, up to ~4 min)
